summary.headline: The School Committee approved the Neary feasibility study bid document, reviewed the $8.8 million Trottier roof project, and held an FY27 budget hearing.
summary.summary: The Southborough School Committee held a public hearing on its proposed $26,114,718 FY27 operating budget, an increase of 3.99% over FY26. Members approved bid specifications for an architectural feasibility study on renovations to Margaret A. Neary Elementary School and discussed forming a joint five-member building committee. The committee also reviewed plans for an $8,833,964 roof replacement at P. Brent Trottier Middle School, which qualifies for an estimated $3,446,336 state grant, and saw a classroom demonstration of a proposed $365,000 capital request for interactive touchscreens.

topics.title: FY27 school operating budget public hearing
topics.summary: The committee held a formal public hearing on the proposed FY27 school operating budget. The proposed operational budget totals $26,114,718, reflecting an increase of $1,001,932, or 3.99%, over FY26. Regular education costs total $18,389,667 (up 6.81%), while special education costs total $7,725,051 (down 2.15%), which includes offsets from the state circuit breaker program.
key_details: Proposed FY27 budget totals $26,114,718, a 3.99% increase over FY26.
Regular day education totals $18,389,667, an increase of 6.81%.
Special education totals $7,725,051, a decrease of 2.15%.
State circuit breaker offsets include $263,850 for special education transportation and $1,403,423 for out-of-district tuitions.
Copies of the budget are available online, at the central office, and at town offices.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 4-0 to close the public hearing.
topics.why_it_matters: The school budget represents a major portion of municipal spending and will be voted on by residents at the April Annual Town Meeting.

topics.title: School updates and student achievements
topics.summary: District administrators reported on recent activities across the four Southborough K-8 schools. Highlights included staff donor recognition at Finn School, cultural presentations and a science program at Woodward School, Youth Art Month recognitions and a student Ramadan presentation at Neary School, and middle school community events at Trottier School.
key_details: Mary E. Finn Elementary School received an employer recognition award from New England Donor Services.
Ten Neary Elementary art students had work selected for the Massachusetts Art Education Association statewide Youth Art Month exhibit.
Trottier Middle School held its first annual Ram Jam school-wide competition and spirit event.
Seventh-grader Jacob Brooks won Trottier Middle School's annual geography bee.
topics.outcome: Information shared; no committee action required.

topics.title: Classroom interactive display demonstration and capital request
topics.summary: District technology staff and second-grade teachers presented a live demonstration of Newline interactive touch displays piloted in second-grade classrooms this year. Existing classroom projectors across the district are 9 to 17 years old, dimming, and increasingly failing. The district is requesting $365,000 at Annual Town Meeting to install interactive displays across all remaining K-8 classrooms.
key_details: ATM capital request totals $365,000: $70,000 for Finn, $40,000 for Woodward, $75,000 for Neary, and $180,000 for Trottier.
Total installed cost averages approximately $3,000 per classroom, including hardware, wiring, and mounting.
Boards feature 4K displays, blue light filters, 20 touch points, and non-proprietary software with no ongoing subscription fees.
The vendor provides a seven-year warranty and free ongoing professional development.
Summer 2025 pilot deployed 62 panels at Algonquin, 20 at Melican, and 7 at Woodward.
topics.outcome: Discussion completed; capital request will appear before voters at the April Annual Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: Approval of the $365,000 capital request would modernize instructional display technology across all Southborough elementary and middle school classrooms.

topics.title: Eureka Math2 curriculum implementation update
topics.summary: District math coordinator Kathy Lizotte updated the committee on the first year of full K-5 implementation of the Eureka Math2 curriculum. The program emphasizes conceptual understanding using concrete-to-pictorial-to-abstract models, math discussions, and vertical alignment across grade levels. Feedback indicates improved coherence and student reasoning, though teachers and math coaches continue refining pacing guides and assessment expectations.
key_details: All K-5 teachers across the district are in full year-one implementation of Eureka Math2.
Teams meet twice monthly in professional learning communities with district math coaches.
The district held two well-attended evening parent information sessions.
Year two priorities include integrating Universal Design for Learning principles and analyzing student assessment data.
Students continue utilizing the supplementary ST Math digital puzzle program about 15 minutes per day.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee addressed regular procedural matters, including accepting a small gift donation, reappointing a committee representative, and approving payroll warrants and meeting minutes.
key_details: Accepted a $40 donation from the American Online Giving Foundation for the Southborough Extended Day Program.
Reappointed Megan Hanley as the School Committee representative to the Municipal Technology Committee.
Approved February payroll warrants and nine vendor warrants.
Approved open meeting minutes for January 30, February 11, and February 26, 2026, and executive session minutes for January 14, 2026.

topics.title: Neary School feasibility study RFS and building committee
topics.summary: Following the approval of $175,000 at the March Special Town Meeting, the committee reviewed the draft Request for Services to hire an architectural and engineering firm for the Neary School feasibility study. The committee approved language targeting a maximum cost of $15 million for deferred maintenance (Option 2), minus the estimated $4.5 million cost of the separate roof replacement. Members also reviewed a draft charge to establish a five-member Southborough Elementary School Building Committee to be appointed jointly with the Select Board.
key_details: The RFS studies two paths: a comprehensive renovation of Neary (Option 1) and deferred maintenance up to $15 million less the roof replacement (Option 2).
RFS schedule sets a consultant site visit for March 23 and proposals due on April 2.
The committee proposed that the building committee consist of five voting members jointly appointed by the School Committee and Select Board.
School Committee members plan to meet jointly with the Select Board on March 17 to finalize the committee charge.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 4-0 to approve the Neary feasibility study Request for Services bid document with amendments.
topics.why_it_matters: The feasibility study will determine the long-term renovation or maintenance plan for Neary Elementary School, with major budget and facility implications for the town.

topics.title: New principal appointments for Neary and Finn schools
topics.summary: Superintendent Gregory Martineau announced the hiring of two new school principals starting in the 2026-2027 school year. Tom Collett was appointed principal of Neary Elementary School, and Deb Lemieux was appointed principal of Mary E. Finn Elementary School. Both leaders are participating in transition and onboarding activities this spring.
key_details: Tom Collett will succeed Kathleen Valenti as principal of Margaret A. Neary Elementary School.
Deb Lemieux will succeed Clayton Ryan as principal of Mary E. Finn Elementary School.
Both candidates are beginning onboarding and transition visits to meet faculty, students, and families.

topics.title: Trottier Middle School roof replacement project update
topics.summary: Assistant Superintendent Keith Lavoie presented an update on the proposed P. Brent Trottier Middle School roof replacement project heading to Annual Town Meeting as Article 15. The Massachusetts School Building Authority approved the project scope under its Accelerated Repair Program with a 41.32% reimbursement rate. Administrators shared photographs showing leaks, buckled substrate plywood, and internal diverter bladders used to manage water leaks across the 1998 building.
key_details: Total estimated gross project cost is $8,833,964.
Estimated MSBA grant is $3,446,336, leaving an estimated net cost to Southborough of $5,387,628.
The 1998 roof is experiencing active leaks, buckled decking, and deteriorated gutters that pitch away from drains.
Project approval requires a two-thirds vote at Town Meeting on April 11 and a ballot vote in May.
If approved, construction is projected for spring/summer 2027.
topics.outcome: Informational update; the article will go before voters at Annual Town Meeting and on the town ballot.
topics.why_it_matters: Residents will vote whether to borrow approximately $8.8 million to replace the Trottier roof, with the state reimbursing over $3.4 million.

topics.title: FY26 budget forecast and revolving fund accounts
topics.summary: Business Administrator Rebecca Pellegrino reported on the FY26 budget through February 28, 2026, showing an available balance of $55,271 (0.22% of the budget), down $88,000 from the prior month due to unexpected staff leaves, long-term substitutes, and an out-of-district placement change. The facility rental revolving account dropped to approximately $24,000 after paying $97,000 in emergency repairs and encumbering $85,000 for the Neary roof project, though a subsequent rental payment brought it back to roughly $40,000.
key_details: FY26 general fund projected remaining balance was $55,271 as of February 28.
Two function codes were overspent: professional development substitutes ($52.50) and grounds maintenance ($527 for ice melt).
Emergency facility repairs in FY26 included $85,000 for Neary roof design work and $10,000 boiler repair deductible.
Kindergarten enrollment for next year stands at 131 students, maintaining seven planned sections within class-size guidelines.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 4-0 to accept the FY26 General Fund report and approve the overexpended function codes.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing on the FY27 budget
Approve the Neary School feasibility study Request for Services bid document with amendments
Accept the FY26 Monthly General Fund report as of February 28, 2026, and approve the overexpended function codes

public_comment.summary: A resident urged the committee to communicate actively, regularly, and transparently with voters regarding capital projects and next steps leading into Town Meeting, rather than relying on last-minute outreach.
